note: Derived reading aid. Never authoritative; never read as intent (Decision 0004). The Plan document governs.
author: Lightweight model draft for Clara (technical writing) via Claudia Atlas <claudia.atlas@agents.arcadia.local>
title: Turn each operator decision into one pinned card
purpose: Every operator decision in a production run should be one pinned card on a remote page, with its consequence and evidence shown. A handoff from one Plan to the next should run through a recorded close-out and a deterministic selector, so it is safe and auditable.
serves: The Project outcome of the operator deciding quickly, and only when needed, during production runs.
done_when: The operator can act on each decision from one card with one button, a stale card is refused with its reason, and a finished Plan hands off to a selected next Plan from a saved close-out record.
reading_note: By operator direction of 2026-10-14, several Actions are held behind three production-path Actions.

actions.title: Define one card format for every operator touch
actions.why: One format for merges, buttons and decisions lets a deterministic engine handle each kind in turn.
actions.done_when: A card with a missing consequence, missing pin or unknown verb is rejected, and a stale pin is refused when the card is used.

actions.title: Create cards from decisions, scripts and pull requests
actions.why: The operator already decides through these three surfaces; cards give them one evidence format readable in under a minute.
actions.done_when: Each of the three sources yields a valid card, the card's pinned fingerprint changes when its source changes, and the source itself is not altered.

actions.title: Show cards with their consequence and one button
actions.why: The operator acts from the pages already in use, and sees the consequence before pressing.
actions.done_when: Each card shows its consequence, evidence links and one verb button, and a stale card shows a refusal with the reason.

actions.title: Record standing approvals for classes of work
actions.why: Approving a policy instead of each instance reduces clicks without widening authority.
actions.done_when: A policy has a class, scope, expiry and evidence requirement, and sensitive classes such as credentials and spend can never match.

actions.title: Write a close-out record at the end of each plan
actions.why: A saved record is what makes handing off to the next Plan safe and auditable.
actions.done_when: The same inputs always give the same record, which lists outcomes, open items, blockers and a recommended successor, and a malformed record fails the check.

actions.title: Select the next plan and check it before starting
actions.why: A handoff between plans needs a deterministic first step that changes nothing.
actions.done_when: The selector names the chosen plan with reasons, refuses a plan authored in the same run or not yet approved, and a failed check names its remedy.

actions.title: Clear a blocked run from its card
actions.why: Clearing these blockers currently needs the command line, and an open alert stands in front of every production run.
actions.done_when: A card clears an environment or budget blocker through a script that pins the blocker and leaves a receipt, and never resets a budget it was not pinned to.

actions.title: Require a test for each fixed friction
actions.why: A friction marked fixed with no test can quietly come back.
actions.done_when: The check fails when a fixed friction cites no test or rule, and a template turns a recorded friction into a failing rehearsal.

actions.title: Show every pull request awaiting the operator on one card
actions.why: Merges are the largest remaining operator touch, so one card and one button per round reduces effort.
actions.done_when: The card lists each pull request with why it needs the operator, its authority boundary, review verdict, checks and consequence, and stacked pull requests are ordered base first.

actions.title: Let a card's default run at expiry unless vetoed
actions.why: A default that runs at expiry spares the operator routine cards, while a veto keeps control with them.
actions.done_when: A card's default runs at expiry only when no veto was recorded, a veto before expiry cancels it, and sensitive classes can never declare a default.

actions.title: Count each operator touch and its latency
actions.why: Shows how much operator attention each run actually needs, so the target can be measured.
actions.done_when: Each card verb writes a touch record, and the production page shows touches per Action, median decision time and the share answered from the card alone.

actions.title: Connect the batch merge card to the to-do page
actions.why: The batch button must refuse an unsafe batch rather than merge stale work.
actions.done_when: The button posts only the card and head revision of each pull request, and refuses the whole batch with a reason if any head moved, a check is not green or a review is missing.

actions.title: Publish the batch merge script and its Discord ping
actions.why: A published script keeps merges reviewable and out of the agents' hands.
actions.done_when: The batch merge runs as a published operator script, writes one receipt per pull request, is safe to re-run, and a pending batch posts one Discord message linking the card.

actions.title: Order the next steps by what unblocks work
actions.why: The operator should first see the step that moves work forward.
actions.done_when: The to-do page lists each waiting pull request as a step in stack order, names its one click, and shows exactly one step to do now.

actions.title: Write each log entry to its own file
actions.why: Parallel branches that add to one shared log cause merge conflicts.
actions.done_when: Two branches that each add a session row, a friction entry and a hand-off update merge in either order without conflict.

actions.title: Write a short protocol for the lead and implementer pair
actions.why: A new lead session should run the pair loop correctly from its first turn.
actions.done_when: A protocol of at most one page states how findings, implementer continuity and fresh reviewers work, and a new lead session can run it unaided.
